candidates.original_title: Improving problem solving with subgoal labels in procedural instructions and worked examples
candidates.description: Subgoal labeled expository text interacts with subgoal labeled worked examples to improve problem solving performance in chemistry
candidates.citation_sentence: The present study used methods similar to those described in Margulieux and Catrambone (2016).
candidates.notes: Experiment 2 replicated the original programming study in the chemistry domain; the key interaction effect was not found (F(1,116)=0.79, p=0.38) and the pattern of results differed from the original programming study, with subgoal labeled expository text showing a marginal main effect rather than the original interaction pattern. Experiment 2 tested the replication in chemistry (reaction stoichiometry). Subgoal labeled expository text improved performance on its own, contrary to the original finding that text alone did not help. The key interaction pattern from the original programming study was not replicated. Authors state 'the results were not the hypothesized results.'
